items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: And we became very close friends ever after that. He and I and Doc West used to live in the same place... Doc was the official cook for the group... we had a ball.

ctx.x: That was my tune. So he and I and Doc West were... I was living actually on 25th Street, but they lived on 28th Street (that's on the east side), and I used to be there so much until I considered myself living there, too. We used to just hang out together. And there was an old raggedy piano, and I sat down one day and played "Pastels," which when I wrote it was called "Please Let Me Forget." It was actually my torch for some girl I had been in love with who didn't know I was alive.

items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: and Erroll, Harold West, and a bunch of other people. Then the record band started. This was in '47.

ctx.x: and Erroll, Harold West, and a bunch of other people. Then the record band started. This was in '47. So C.P. Johnson, who had had a band around town that I had been writing for, gets a gig in Honolulu...or not Honolulu but all the islands. So Trummy Young and Dexter and I, and Ulysses Livingston, and Arthur Dennis (and I can't think of the trumpeter's name at the moment), we all go to Honolulu. So just the day before we go to Honolulu, C.P. gets busted for marijuana. And the headlines when we get to Honolulu is,…
That was all you stayed in that one...
